card.title: PS5 Main Power Rail Low Resistance Diagnosed as Shorted High-Side MOSFET

source.title: Stop Injecting Voltage Until You Check This! — nanofix

symptoms: Low resistance on main power rail
Suspicious non-zero short resistance (e.g., 0.4 ohms to 15 o

claims.statement: A low resistance or apparent short on the main 12V power rail is often caused by a shorted high-side MOSFET in a buck regulator rather than a direct short to ground.
claims.evidence: Resistance measurements between the main power rail and buck regulator outputs show continuity through a failed dual MOSFET.

claims.statement: Injecting voltage into the main power rail when a high-side MOSFET is shorted will feed 12V directly into sensitive components like the SOC.
claims.evidence: The high-side MOSFET shorts drain to source, bridging the 12V input directly to the switching node and the SOC rail.

claims.statement: Check the resistance between the main power rail and the outputs of downstream buck regulator inductors to safely identify a shorted MOSFET before injecting voltage.
claims.evidence: Checking inductor outputs reveals whether the low resistance originates from a buck converter stage rather than a standard ground short.

claims.statement: A shorted high-side MOSFET can sometimes allow 12V to reach the SOC without permanently destroying it if protective measures or shut-downs occurred in time.
claims.evidence: Replacing the shorted MOSFET and the shorted South Bridge restored full functionality to the console.

procedure: {'step': 'Measure the resistance on the main power rail to determine if a low resistance or dead short is present.'}
{'step': 'Check the resistance between the main power rail and the output side of known downstream buck regulator inductors.'}
{'step': 'Verify if there is direct continuity or very low resistance between the 12V input and the switching node of the dual MOSFETs.'}
{'step': 'Identify and replace any shorted dual MOSFETs or associated damaged ICs (such as the South Bridge) before applying power or voltage.'}

measurements.point: Main power rail to ground (resistance mode)
measurements.context: Apparent dead short or low resistance

measurements.point: Main power rail to ground (diode mode)
measurements.context: Voltage drop showing apparent dead short

measurements.point: Main power rail to buck regulator output inductor

cautions: SOURCE RISK: Injecting voltage directly onto the main power rail without checking for a shorted high-side MOSFET can feed 12V into the SOC and permanently destroy the board.
card.caveats: A low resistance reading on a main power rail does not automatically mean a direct short to ground; always verify downstream buck converter outputs first.
